spec.name: Trend v30
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.4, annual return 5%, maximum drawdown 11%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.42 to 1.48 (change +0.05).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.42 to 1.42. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.40 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.42); it breaks even at 114.7 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.42 against 1.42 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 2.10 against 1.42 in research, a gap of -0.68.
The best year gives 40% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 254%; Sharpe is 5.41 in calm and -7.44 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.12, so the claimed 1.40 becomes 1.28 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.53 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.03, 95th percentile 0.47).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.42 to as low as 1.51 (as low as 1.63 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (21 days) give 31% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 23% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
